title: Sara Duterte says resignation 'out of the question' amid impeachment trial
summary: Vice President Sara Duterte on Friday reiterated that she would not be stepping down from office amid her impeachment trial.

blocks.text: Published November 27, 2026 5:01pm
Vice President Sara Duterte on Friday reiterated that she would not be stepping down from office amid her impeachment trial.
“No, sir. Resignation, that is out of the question. I already answered that several times during the course of the trial,” Duterte said in a press conference.

“It is something that I cannot do because I feel that it's a betrayal of the 32.2 million people who voted for me, and of course the general public, if I resign from the position of Vice President,” she added.

The Vice President is currently facing an impeachment trial before the Senate impeachment court.

Her defense team has been presenting evidence and witnesses for Article II of the impeachment case, alleging her unexplained wealth due to her supposed failure to truthfully disclose assets in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN), and failure to divest in businesses as constitutionally required for the President and Vice President.
Preparing for worst
Duterte also admitted that she and her defense team are always “preparing for the worst” now that the trial is nearing its end and the Senate impeachment court is expected to issue a verdict soon.

“Because if there's an acquittal, it will just be a continuation of what we are doing now for the Office of the Vice President. So next year, all the projects and all the programs will be implemented as if it's 2026 or 2025 or 2024—a matter of difference of budget,” she explained.
“But if it's a verdict of guilty, it will come with a lot of consequences,” she added.
The Vice President said her primary concern, if she is ever convicted in her impeachment trial, is the expected loss of employment in the OVP.
She said around 300 families of employees from various OVP satellite offices across the country may be affected by the possible conviction.
“Because the satellite offices are coterminous to me as Vice President. So that is our first worry, the jobs of those OVP employees who are coterminous,” she said.
Duterte also said she is preparing to ask those stationed in the OVP headquarters in Mandaluyong City to move out if she gets convicted.
“So those are the things that we need to prepare for. But if it's a verdict of acquittal, then we don't have to prepare for anything except for the rollout of projects for 2027,” she said.
Acceptance
Nevertheless, Duterte said she will accept whatever the decision will be at the end of the trial—whether she will get acquitted or convicted.

“We will accept whatever it is that the judgment of the Senate impeachment court will give for the impeachment trial, and we will all have to live with the consequences of this out-of-mind decision of President Marcos,” she said.
Malacañang has repeatedly said that President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. is not influencing the impeachment proceedings against the Vice President.—AOL, GMA News
